 By Madison Kemeny | MKemeny@syracuse.com 
 “Dancing With the Stars” airs its emotional Dedication Night tonight, Tuesday, Oct. 20, at 8 p.m. ET on ABC and Disney+. The 10 remaining couples will honor the people and places that shaped their lives. Kym Johnson, a two-time Mirrorball champion, returns as guest judge.
 This week is also the first known pro suspension in the show’s history. Val Chmerkovskiy is sitting out, so his partner Jenna Dewan will dance with Alan Bersten.
 Don’t have cable or an over-the-air antenna? New customers can watch “Dancing with the Stars” for free with DIRECTV’s 5-day trial through its signature packages and eligible genre packs, or Fubo’s free trial , both of which include ABC access.

 Each couple’s dance is dedicated to someone special. Last year the celebrities were joined on the dance floor by family and friends for the first time, and ABC plans the same this year.
 Stiles is dedicating her routine to her late “10 Things I Hate About You” co-star Ledger, who died in 2008 at age 28.
 The show will also feature a dance to Hilary Duff’s “CATastrophe” from “The Cat in the Hat.” A dedication performance to Dolly Parton will be set to “Here You Come Again” by Parton and Willa Amai. Pro and troupe routines are set to “Fever Dream” by Alex Warren and “Stay (If You Wanna Dance)” by Myles Smith.
 Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough return as judges, and Alfonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough co-host.

 Why Val Chmerkovskiy is sitting out
 After the Oct. 13 show, Inaba critiqued Johnson for a lift in her routine with Shum Jr. and read the definition of a lift. Chmerkovskiy then posted a TikTok story that read, “You almost saw Fresh Prince enter the ballroom last night.” The post was widely viewed as a reference to Will Smith slapping Chris Rock at the 2022 Oscars.
 He deleted the post and apologized. BBC Studios, per ABC News , which produces the show, said the post “was inappropriate and does not reflect the values or standards expected of anyone connected with the show.”
 Chmerkovskiy said he made “a poor decision” while trying to defend his wife. ABC News reported that Dewan is aware of the change and has continued to be professional and respectful of the process.
 What happened last week on ‘Dancing With the Stars’
 Week 5 was the show’s first-ever Super Bowl Night . Couples danced to songs from past halftime shows, and “Monday Night Football” announcer Joe Buck served as guest judge.
 Dewan and Chmerkovskiy scored the first all-9s of the season, a 36 out of 40 for a paso doble to “Bad Romance.” Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach tied them with a salsa. Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov were next with 34.
 Guillermo Rodriguez of “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” and pro Witney Carson were eliminated after a salsa to Bad Bunny’s “Tití Me Preguntó.” They scored 22 out of 40, the lowest of the night . He had been saved by viewer votes in earlier weeks.
 “Witney, I love you for teaching me how to dance,” Rodriguez said as he left.

 How to vote for ‘Dancing With the Stars’
 Eliminations combine judges’ scores with viewer votes. You can vote two ways:
 Online: Go to DWTSVote.abc.com, then choose your couples and click “Save Votes.” Online voting is open to eligible viewers in the U.S., its territories and Canada.
 By text: Send a couple’s keyword to 21523. Keywords are shown during the live broadcast and are typically a variation of the celebrity’s name. Text voting is limited to the U.S. and its territories on participating carriers.
 Viewers must be 18 or older. You get up to 10 votes per couple through each method, which means up to 20 per couple.
 Voting opens when the live show begins at 8 p.m. ET and closes shortly after the final performance. West Coast viewers need to vote during that live window instead of waiting for their local airing. Votes can’t be cast during on-demand viewing.
